## Single-input HTML report

Prepare report data once, then write a CSV-backed HTML page:

```r
report <- validation_report_data(result, model)
write_validation_results(report, "report")
write_validation_report(report, "report/report.html")
```

The Abstract shows the input, versions, status, and error/warning counts. Zero counts and skipped checks are hidden.

Summary and Validation messages start with a severity icon and a labelled stage
icon (Structure, Field, Business). All sheets appear in Validation messages,
including fixed-cell sheets and workbook-level problems. CSV exports retain
plain severity and stage text; the CSV files include explicit report metadata.

Summary and Validation messages use sheet tabs with search, column filters, pagination, and CSV buttons.

Table summaries group identical field, column, value, severity, stage, and message combinations, with occurrence counts.

Fixed-cell findings appear individually in Summary. Validation messages retains every finding for every sheet.

“Checks that could not finish” lists only incomplete or failed checks and is hidden when empty.

An unfinished validation never appears as a successful report, even with no error findings.

CSV and HTML reuse the prepared report’s formatted tables.

The HTML loads adjacent `summary.csv` and `findings.csv` over HTTP.
Publish both CSV files and the `report-assets` folder with the HTML.
Apache or a Shiny static resource directory can serve the files.
No rendering packages, Pandoc, or external CDN are required.
For collections, set `assets_directory` to a shared relative directory.

The original workbook is not copied. Existing report files require explicit `overwrite = TRUE`.

`validation_report_data()` returns plain tables for reuse by a future Shiny interface, without rendering or revalidation.

CSV exports include all recorded problems, explicit structure status and UTC generation time.
Prepared reports also export finding stages, field labels, sheet order and layout.
